bottleneck: Neuromorphic chips promise brain-like efficiency, but they are designed around oversimplified neuron models because the brain's true computational primitives are unknown. Without knowing what to copy — spike timing, dendritic computation, neuromodulation, glial signaling — engineers copy the easy parts (leaky integrate-and-fire units) and miss the algorithm. The result is hardware efficient at the wrong computations: impressive energy numbers on benchmarks that do not capture what brains actually do. Hardware built on a wrong abstraction of neural computation cannot converge on brain-like capability no matter how it scales.
current_state: Intel Loihi and IBM NorthPole cut energy use dramatically for narrow tasks, but no neuromorphic system approaches general brain-like computation, and the primitive question is rarely addressed.

sources.title: Brain Connectome: Mapping Neural Networks in Neuroscience

title: Neuromorphic chips copy unknown primitives
why_it_blocks: Energy-efficient AI needs the brain's tricks, but we are reverse-engineering a machine whose instruction set we have not read. Hardware without the algorithm is premature optimization on a planetary energy budget.
